assertion_analysis.fails_if: an explicit f=1 or cross-field argument changes any solution field, because the explicit solve is compared bit-exactly with the omitted-fill solve; it would not redden if the unit-fill branch merely appended the same operands, so it guards the API and the default path rather than the division itself.

the gain term, either component order of N, the per-cell fill or the iron_magnetisation division is wrong; the expected value comes from an independent elimination of the internal iron field, not from the solver.
a zero or >1 fill, a two-component fill, a negative or >1 factor or a non-finite value is accepted, because the interaction assembly is poisoned to prove the refusal precedes assembly.
the gain is dropped from the residual; the same point scores zero with the gain and more than 0.1 of the reference norm without it.

either receipt error passes its 10%/11% bound, proven by raising the stored row to limit+1e-6 and requiring the refusal, and it also fails if the receipt stops asserting the H200 device or the 0.4 factor.
the one-third smear ratio check is removed or loosened, proven by doubling the smear error to a 0.5 ratio and requiring the refusal.
the section factor stops improving on the plain fill by at least half on the 0.10 m grid; it cannot fail on the absolute bound, which the gate moved to the 0.032 m receipt.
the tolerance is reverted to a zero absolute allowance (rejecting 1e-16-of-scale noise) or loosened past a 1e-9 relative change of a dominant element.
the affine factor stops matching the differentiated projected law, e.g. if the gain diagonal or the per-node fill factor is dropped from _linear_factor; the check runs at fill 1.0 and 0.2.
the affine basis loses the per-cell fill or cross-field tensor; the expected coefficients come from the analytic effective susceptibility and the generalised Gram solve, independent of the solver.

evidence_caveats: The fine-grid acceptance is asserted from the external receipt /work/projects/imas_gpu/sophelio/evidence/iron-limb-fill/production/material-refinement-20261114/summary.json, not recomputed by a test; I re-read it (sha256 dfa2a73d5e4b7bcadd098a0e1052d2ec7d8cf57aff3bc08350ffebfe0b07a66f) and its 0.032 m rows reproduce geometry 0.052446/0.106595 and smear 0.427729/0.499785 with device NVIDIA H200 NVL.

The control gate receipt was recorded at head_revision c5d1b1c5606e2ba4106f80bbf5a2e053e0742c2f while the receipt rows themselves are stamped 8ab69e765a812f1713129852eb65e4b5d886f26d; I diffed nova/biot/magnetisation.py from 8ab69e76 to 55d76179 and found the constant-basis residual, coefficient and material resolution unchanged, which is what makes those rows applicable to the reviewed head.

The production gate arm is recorded passed: false with production exit 1 in production-gate-receipt.json because measure.py:240 applies the 10% bound to the 0.05/0.1 m arms, which read 12.6% and 24.2% at mu=200; the node therefore relies on the control gate validator for the fine-grid acceptance rather than a green production arm.

The dispatch fence said at most ten Newton corrections while plan section 2 and the restated receipt say fifteen; the recorded WEST corrections are 6 at 0.08 m and 12 at 0.04 m with terminal residual 1.387e-12 at 0.04 m.

added_failure_count is derived from the reviewed run's gate logs: baseline-suite.log ends '53 passed in 4595.82s' with EXIT=0 and merge-head-suite.log ends '83 passed in 7948.20s' with EXIT=0 and 0 compatibility mismatches, so no failure id is added.

item_verdicts.diff: I read the 20 node commits from bf61ef594ce36cb3fb75cbf57fc592e1185ffd4f to 5b63d8e79ced75662e165a0a40154e09f5be2bc5 (+1517/-4 across ten files) and the merge 55d761795a8878ac842f39cba35dbb091f11617d against its first parent (+197/-16 in nova/biot/magnetisation.py, +321 in tests/test_magnetisation.py), which preserves the fill and cross-field keywords and applies them to the affine basis the primary branch brought in.
item_verdicts.done_when: The quantitative clauses are the 10%/11% fine-grid bound with the one-third smear reduction, unit-fill invariance, the solid f=1 control, the two-cell-size ratio table and the WEST 1e-8 correction budget; scripts/iron_limb_production/gate.py:44-54 asserts the first two against a recorded H200 receipt, tests/test_magnetisation.py:1038-1046 and scripts/iron_limb_production/compatibility.py:64 assert unit-fill invariance, and the corrections 6 at 0.08 m and 12 at 0.04 m are recorded in the external receipts, but the solid control and ratio table are unasserted (see finding at gate.py:44).
item_verdicts.goal: The dispatched goal is a per-cell toroidal fill fraction and cross-field factor in the production axisymmetric iron solve; nova/biot/magnetisation.py:632-635 takes both as scalar, (cells,) or centroid-callback arguments, nova/biot/magnetisation.py:443-452 applies fill and gain in the constant residual, nova/biot/magnetisation.py:477-495 applies them at affine quadrature nodes, and nova/biot/magnetisation.py:565-573 exposes the iron magnetisation and the stored material fields.
item_verdicts.manifest: The manifest records status complete, 20 commits, ten changed paths, baseline-suite.log at bf61ef59 (53 passed, EXIT=0) and merge-head-suite.log at 55d76179 (83 passed, EXIT=0, 68 baseline captures compared with 0 compatibility mismatches), with the fine-grid acceptance 5.244561%/10.659474% and the WEST budget receipt at 15 corrections; its after_suite cites the repaired merge-head arm rather than the earlier failing after-suite.log, and the provenance correction in suites-gate-receipt.json discloses that substitution.
item_verdicts.write_paths: The reviewed manifest declares nova/biot/magnetisation.py, tests/test_magnetisation.py, scripts/iron_limb_production, docs/evidence/fragments/iron-limb-fill-fraction and docs/figures/iron-limb-fill-fraction/ilf-material-fill-fraction; the node's ten changed files all lie inside those grants, and the merge commit's resolution touches only nova/biot/magnetisation.py and tests/test_magnetisation.py.

justifications.durability: tests/test_magnetisation.py:1054 and :1509 derive the expected per-cell tensor by eliminating the internal iron field independently, and tests/test_magnetisation.py:1157/1181 raise the stored error, so reinstating a dropped gain, a wrong component order or a loosened bound reddens them; the plan's 1e-12 omission invariance still rides on scripts/iron_limb_production/compatibility.py:64, whose baseline capture is not committed.
justifications.evidence: scripts/iron_limb_production/gate.py:44-54 asserts bounds 0.10/0.11 and a 1/3 smear ratio against an H200 receipt whose 0.032 m rows I re-read (geometry 0.052446/0.106595, smear 0.427729/0.499785), but gate.py:24 never reads the receipt's revision and gate.py:44 never asserts the solid f=1 or ratio-table controls the done-when names.
justifications.fit: The additions follow the surrounding dataclass, keyword-only and jnp idioms of nova/biot/magnetisation.py and introduce no name the repository rules forbid; the gate's acceptance logic is written with bare assert statements at scripts/iron_limb_production/gate.py:25-54, which vanish under python -O.
justifications.goal_fidelity: nova/biot/magnetisation.py:632-635 carries fill_fraction and cross_field_factor on the public solve, scripts/iron_limb_production/measure.py:61-73 solves every control and WEST arm through them, and the merge at 55d76179 keeps both keywords beside the affine basis rather than replacing them.
justifications.reuse: I searched nova for an existing cell-material resolver (def *_material*, callable-field resolution, CellSizeField) and for a reference-scaled close comparison (nova/imas, nova/equilibrium, nova/transport) and found no owner of either capability; the affine machinery is imported from its owner nova/biot/tiledassembly rather than reimplemented, and _cell_material and assert_compatible extend this module rather than fork a second mechanism.
justifications.scope_discipline: The ten files in the node diff are inside the declared grants and the merge resolution is confined to nova/biot/magnetisation.py and tests/test_magnetisation.py; the 359-file first-parent diff at the merge carries the primary branch only.
